root_cause: The cluster autoscaler's nightly scale-down of the spot user pool picks one node at 02:00-04:00 and evicts every pod on it in one pass; two of the three zookeeper replicas are co-located on that node, no PodDisruptionBudget exists in the streaming namespace (kubectl-get-pdb.txt: none), and the pod template sets no cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict annotation — so the ensemble loses 2 of 3 members simultaneously and quorum falls until the evicted replicas reschedule and rejoin ~40 minutes later.
evidence: cluster-autoscaler.log: at 02:20:06 the autoscaler evicts streaming/zookeeper-1 and streaming/zookeeper-2 together from the one node chosen for removal
kubectl-get-pdb.txt: no PodDisruptionBudget exists in the streaming namespace, so nothing caps simultaneous zookeeper disruptions
statefulset.yaml: pod template has no safe-to-evict annotation and no topology rule keeping replicas apart, so two replicas share a removable node
zookeeper.log: 02:20:12 the remaining replica logs 'only 1 of 3 ensemble members reachable' and exits on quorum loss, recurring 02:00-04:00 on 10/25, 10/22, 10/18
fix: Add a PodDisruptionBudget (minAvailable: 2) for the zookeeper StatefulSet and set pod template annotations cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false" (plus pod anti-affinity to spread replicas), so the autoscaler cannot evict two replicas at once — it will drain a node that keeps the quorum intact instead.
